Southern Swedish Forest Research Centre
Third-cycle subject area
Forest Management
Description of the doctoral project
 
Douglas-fir is a promising alternative for diversifying Swedish production forests under a changing climate. Its wider use requires better knowledge of needle diseases that can cause needle loss, crown thinning and reduced growth. This four-year PhD project will investigate how host genetics, fungal communities and environmental conditions influence Douglas-fir health and productivity. It will examine disease patterns across Swedish growing conditions, identify the fungi involved and explore genetic variation in a major needle-disease pathogen. The project will also investigate differences in resistance and tolerance among provenances and how disease affects growth. The aim is to support the selection of suitable planting material and sites for future forestry.
The project is based at the Southern Swedish Forest Research Centre in Alnarp, in collaboration with Skogforsk, Södra and international researchers. The doctoral student will join a multidisciplinary forestry research environment. The project combines field surveys and established forestry trials with fungal diagnostics, sequencing and population genetics analysis.
 
About the position
The doctoral student will plan and conduct field and laboratory studies, manage and analyse data, write scientific papers and a doctoral thesis, and communicate results through conferences and dialogue with project partners. Work includes field surveys and sampling at sites across Sweden, microscopy, fungal isolation and culturing, molecular identification, sequencing-based analyses and statistical modelling. The student will complete relevant doctoral courses and progressively develop independence in research planning, analysis and scientific writing.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in Forest Management. To meet the specific entry requirements, you must have at least 90 credits in subjects relevant to Forest Management, including at least 30 credits at second-cycle level. 
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
Your profile
We are looking for a motivated candidate with a strong interest in forest pathology and in how tree genetics and environmental conditions influence disease and forest productivity.
Required qualifications:
University education in forestry is essential. Applicants must have a Master’s degree in forestry or forest science, or an equivalent degree with a substantial forestry component, and meet the eligibility requirements above.
Documented practical experience in forest pathology, acquired through a degree project, research or relevant employment, including assessment or diagnosis of fungal diseases of forest trees.
A sound understanding of forest ecology and silviculture, and basic competence in experimental design and statistical data analysis.
Ability to communicate scientific work clearly in spoken and written English.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively, organise field and laboratory work, and undertake fieldwork involving travel within Sweden.
The following are considered merits:
Experience of forest health surveys, disease assessment, needle or crown condition assessments, or work in forestry field trials.
Experience of microscopy, fungal isolation and culturing, or morphological identification of fungi.
Experience of DNA extraction, PCR, sequence-based fungal identification or other molecular diagnostic methods.
Experience of high-throughput sequencing, ITS metabarcoding, bioinformatics or analysis of fungal community data.
Knowledge of population genetics, molecular markers, phylogenetic analysis or pathogen population structure.
Experience of statistical analysis in R or comparable software, particularly mixed models, multivariate analysis, or integration of climate, site and growth data.
Knowledge of Swedish or another Scandinavian language, or willingness to learn Swedish, and a valid driving licence.
About us
The Southern Swedish Forest Research Centre conducts research and teaching on sustainable forestry, with expertise in silviculture, forest ecology, forest pathology, forest policy and planning. We work closely with partners in the forest sector and offer a collegial, international research environment at SLU’s Alnarp campus. The doctoral student will join the department’s forest pathology research environment and a multidisciplinary network of researchers and practitioners.

Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/

jobs.description:
Department of Applied Animal Science and Welfare
Third-cycle subject area
Animal Science
Description of the doctoral project
This PhD project aims to establish subjective time perception as a new animal-centred dimension of animal welfare. It combines animal welfare science, ethology, comparative cognition, affective neuroscience and human time-perception research. The project will examine how affective state, predictability and agency influence animals’ temporal experience, using dogs as the principal model species.
About the position
The PhD student will:
conduct a structured interdisciplinary review of time perception and its relevance to animal welfare
adapt, pilot and validate an interval-timing task for dogs
design and conduct experiments examining timing behaviour under neutral, positive and mildly negative affective conditions
train dogs using positive reinforcement and collect behavioural and physiological data
analyse video recordings, operant responses, heart rate, heart-rate variability and salivary cortisol
contribute to the development of a conceptual framework for studying time perception across companion, farm, laboratory and zoo animals
publish the findings in international scientific journals and present them at national and international conferences

You will join an interdisciplinary and international research environment with expertise in animal welfare, animal cognition, and affective states. The position provides opportunities to develop skills in animal experimentation, cognitive testing, behavioural analysis, physiological measurements, statistics and scientific communication.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
The specific entry requirements for the subject animal science are knowledge corresponding to at least 120 higher education credits in biology subjects, of which a total of at least 30 credits must be in animal science. This must include at least 30 credits at advanced level and the student must have demonstrated the ability to work independently in a degree project. Applicants with a different, comparable educational background may be eligible; this will be decided by the faculty board on a case-by case basis.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
Your profile
At the time of employment, you must have completed a Master’s degree, or equivalent, in animal science, biology, ethology, veterinary science, psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience or another relevant subject.
You should have:
a strong interest in animal behaviour, animal welfare and cognition
experience or training in experimental research and quantitative data analysis
experience in ethogram development, behavioural observations and/or video coding
the ability to plan, document and complete research tasks independently
excellent written and spoken English

Experience considered a merit:
handling or training dogs or other animals using positive reinforcement
cognitive or operant testing
collection or analysis of heart-rate variability, cortisol or other physiological data
statistical analysis in R or similar software

As a person, you should be curious, patient, analytical and attentive to detail. You should be comfortable working both independently and collaboratively and have a responsible and ethically sensitive approach to research involving animals. Good organisational and communication skills are important because the project involves collaboration across scientific disciplines and with international research partners.

The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) has a key role in the development for sustainable life, based on science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and the responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable societal development and good living conditions on our planet. Our main campuses are located in Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, however, the university also operates at research stations, experimental forests and teaching sites throughout Sweden. SLU has around 4,000 employees, 6,000 students and doctoral students and a turnover of over SEK 4,5 billion. We are investing in attractive environments on all of our campuses. We strive to provide a work environment characterised by inclusivity and gender equality, where different experiences generate conversations between people and pave the way for science, creativity and development. Therefore, we welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

Department of Biosystems and Technology
Third-cycle subject area: Agricultural Science
PhD Project: Sustainability Assessment of Agroecological Farming Systems
Description of the doctoral project
The PhD project is a collaboration between the Animal Centred Environments group and the Horticultural and Agroecological Systems (HAS) subject area within the Department. The doctoral research will focus on sustainability assessment of agroecological livestock farming systems, drawing on expertise across both groups and involving collaboration with researchers, farmers and other stakeholders across Europe and Africa through ALASTRA and STRONG MCSA.
About the position
How can sustainability assessment support the transition to more resilient and sustainable farming systems? This PhD project will investigate how multi-criteria approaches can capture the environmental, economic and social performance of agroecological farming systems, identify synergies and trade-offs, and support decisions by farmers and other agricultural stakeholders.
The doctoral student will work primarily within ALASTRA (Agroecology Living Labs in Africa: Redefining the Role of Animals in Food Systems for Climate Action and Sustainability), an EU-funded Horizon Europe project. ALASTRA brings together researchers, farmers and other stakeholders to co-design and evaluate agroecological livestock farming practices through living labs in Kenya, Tanzania, Tunisia and Zambia. SLU leads the development of the holistic assessment framework, including the selection of indicators and the design of sampling and data collection protocols.
The doctoral student will contribute to developing, adapting and evaluating this framework. The research will draw on approaches such as the Global Farm Metric and established agroecological assessment tools, including OASISm the PG tool and TAPE.
The doctoral student will also contribute to STRONG MCSA, an EU-funded Erasmus+ project that strengthens agricultural stakeholders’ capacity to use multi-criteria sustainability assessment (MCSA). These activities will provide a complementary foundation for the doctoral research in ALASTRA.
The doctoral project will combine literature-based research, development and evaluation of assessment methods, quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and engagement with farmers, advisors and researchers. The student will collaborate with partners in Europe and Africa, contribute to project workshops and scientific publications, and communicate findings to academic and practitioner audiences. International visits and participation in project activities may form part of the doctoral studies.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
The following specific entry requirements apply: For the subject of agricultural science, the applicant must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.

A good understanding of agricultural systems, agroecology and sustainability challenges
Experience in research methods and quantitative data analysis, demonstrated through a degree project or equivalent work
Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within an international, multidisciplinary team

Desirable qualifications
Knowledge or experience of Multi Criteria Sustainability Assessment (MCSA), Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), indicator development or farm assessment tools
Experience with literature reviews and the comparative analysis of methods or tools
Experience with statistical analysis and software such as R, or with qualitative research methods
Knowledge of livestock farming, grazing systems, soil health or agroecological transitions
Experience collaborating with farmers, advisors or other agricultural stakeholders, including participatory research or workshops
Experience working in African agricultural contexts or other international research settings
Interest or experience in developing training resources and communicating research to practitioners
Good communication skills in Swedish or another Scandinavian language
A valid car driver’s licence recognized in Sweden

jobs.occupation: PhD - Linking Stem Nitrogen Homeostasis to Tree Growth
jobs.description:
Department of Forest Genetics and Plant Physiology
Third-cycle subject area
Plant Biology
Description of the doctoral project
 
Nitrogen is a major determinant of forest productivity, influencing tree growth, biomass accumulation and wood formation. However, the physiological and molecular mechanisms linking nitrogen availability to wood formation and tree growth remain poorly understood. While nitrogen uptake and assimilation have been extensively studied in roots and leaves, much less is known about nitrogen transport and metabolism within the vascular tissues of tree stems. In particular, the role of nitrogen homeostasis in the cambial region, where new wood cells are produced and differentiate, remains largely unexplored. Understanding these processes is important for identifying mechanisms that regulate tree growth and nitrogen use efficiency, with implications for sustainable forest production.
This PhD project aims to establish a mechanistic understanding of how nitrogen transport, uptake and metabolism in the cambial region influence wood formation and growth in aspen (Populus tremula). The research combines plant physiology, molecular biology and systems biology, using approaches such as stable isotope tracing, metabolomics, RNA sequencing, spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, microscopy and mathematical modelling.
About the position
The doctoral student will investigate how nitrogen transport and metabolism in the vascular tissues of aspen (Populus tremula) regulate wood formation, tree growth and nitrogen use efficiency. The research will focus on nitrogen homeostasis in the cambial region, including the vascular cambium and developing xylem, and its relationship to growth and wood properties.
The work will involve physiological experiments with aspen trees, including analysis of nitrogen compounds in xylem sap, stable isotope (^15N) tracing to quantify nitrogen uptake and transport, and spatial metabolomic analyses. These measurements will be combined with RNA sequencing and existing spatial and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify regulatory mechanisms involved in nitrogen homeostasis. The student will also analyse tree growth and wood anatomical and chemical properties, and participate in developing quantitative models linking nitrogen metabolism to growth and nitrogen use efficiency. Functional validation of candidate genes will involve genetically modified aspen trees.
The position offers opportunities to develop expertise in plant physiology, molecular biology, metabolomics, bioinformatics and systems biology through collaboration with researchers from complementary disciplines.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have:
been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification;
satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or
acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).

To meet the specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in biology, you must have equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in biology-related subjects. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
Your profile
The applicant should have a Master's degree in biology, biotechnology, biochemistry, engineering or equivalent. Excellent spoken and written English skills, experience with plants as an experimental system, and knowledge of statistics in, for example, the programming language R or Python are necessary. We attach great importance to the ability of the applicant to collaborate and function well in a strong research environment, an interest in learning new things, and a willingness to individually develop the project in collaboration with the research group, as well as high motivation to pursue doctoral studies. Previous experience with plant nitrogen physiology, trees as a model system, genetics, genomics, or bioinformatics are valuable merits.
About us
The Department of forest genetics and plant physiology is part of Umeå Plant Science Centre (UPSC, https://www.upsc.se/) which is a centre of excellence for experimental plant research and forest biotechnology in Northern Sweden. Our mission is to perform excellent and innovative basic research and generate knowledge that benefits forestry, agriculture, environment and society. We work across a wide range of disciplines in plant science reaching from cell biology to ecophysiology and from basic research to industrial applications. Our common goal is to understand the plants’ ability to grow, adapt and acclimate to a changing world and how we can breed better plants.Read more about staff benefits and life as an SLU employee on https://www.slu.se/om-slu/jobba-pa-slu/

The Impact You'll Make
 
As our new Application Engineer in Sweden, you'll be a key technical partner to our customers and sales team, turning customer needs into practical drive and power conversion solutions. 
 

You'll join a small, experienced Swedish team working across the country. This gives you a broad role with exposure to different customers, industries and applications. Rather than focusing on one specific segment, you'll use your technical expertise where it creates the most value, particularly for key customers and during the pre-sales phase. 

 

You'll support customers from the first technical discussion through solution design, sizing and quotation to implementation. You'll have the independence to manage customer relationships in Sweden while working closely with technical and commercial colleagues across Sweden, Denmark and Norway. 

 

The role offers flexibility in where you work. You can be based in the Stockholm, Linköping, Göteborg or Malmö area, including locations within reasonable travelling distance, and combine homeworking with customer visits and time at a Danfoss office. 
What You’ll Be Doing
 
Work with customers and our sales team to understand technical requirements and assisting system designs, supporting customer meetings, project scoping and pre-sales discussions. 
Dimension and select frequency converters, drives and power conversion solutions for different applications.
Act as a trusted technical partner to key customers, taking technical ownership of their applications from initial requirements and product selection through technical clarification, verification, implementation and commissioning on site.
Perform technical analyses, testing and evaluations against customer specifications, helping customers and sales colleagues solve technical challenges.
Share your expertise through technical presentations, product and software training, and collaboration with sales, service partners and technical colleagues across Scandinavia. 

 
You'll have regular contact with customers, so travel is a natural part of the role. You can expect 20-30 travel days per year, mainly within Sweden, with occasional travel to Denmark and Norway. 
 
What We're Looking For
We're open to different educational and career paths. What matters most is a strong technical foundation, practical electrical understanding and an interest in working directly with customers. 
 
To succeed in this role, you'll bring: 
A technical background in electrical engineering, automation, mechatronics or a related field. You may also have started your career as an electrician or electrical installer and are now ready for the next step.
Practical electrical knowledge and an interest in motor control, frequency converters, drives and power conversion.
The ability to work independently, translate customer requirements into practical technical solutions and manage different priorities.
Confidence working directly with customers and supporting sales colleagues in technical and pre-sales discussions.
Fluency in Swedish and English, both written and spoken. Swedish is essential for customer collaboration in Sweden, while English is used across our Scandinavian organization. 

 
Experience with drives, frequency converters, power conversion, electrification or similar technologies is an advantage, but not essential. Familiarity with Danfoss Drives products or Salesforce would also be beneficial. 
 
Most importantly, you bring technical curiosity, initiative and a willingness to learn. We value practical experience alongside formal education, so if you've built your expertise through hands-on work combined with further technical learning, we'd encourage you to apply. 
What You'll Get from Us
 
You'll join a small, experienced Swedish team where you'll have significant independence and the opportunity to build close relationships with customers and sales colleagues. At the same time, you'll be part of a wider Scandinavian technical community where knowledge, expertise and assignments are shared across Sweden, Denmark and Norway. 
 
The breadth of the Swedish market means you'll work with different customers and applications rather than being limited to one segment. It's an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise, develop your commercial understanding and take real ownership of customer challenges. 
 
The position offers a flexible hybrid working model, including the possibility of working from home. Depending on where you're based and the needs of the role, your week may combine homeworking, customer visits and time at a Danfoss office. 
 
We'll support your career growth with mentoring, learning opportunities, and access to global career paths. 
 
You'll have the flexibility, autonomy, and support you need to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. 
 
You'll be part of an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds are respected, valued, and empowered to succeed. 
 
You'll receive a competitive rewards package that includes benefits such as an annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, health insurance, and more. As a global company, these benefits vary by country and contract.
Ready to Make a Difference?
 
If you enjoy combining hands-on technical expertise with customer interaction and want the freedom to take ownership of technical challenges, we'd like to hear from you. 
 

You don't need to come from one specific educational or industry background. If you have strong electrical knowledge, enjoy solving technical problems and are motivated to develop your expertise in drives and power conversion, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every preferred qualification. 

 

Apply and help us turn customer challenges into practical drive and power conversion solutions.
